classification.difficultyReason: Use rhombus diagonal properties to identify a 30° right triangle, then apply an exact cosine ratio.

content.prompt: $ABCD$ is a rhombus with sides $10\text{ cm}$. Find $AX$.

spec.description: Unshaded rhombus ABCD with both diagonals intersecting at X. The 60° arc spans the whole angle BAD, crossing diagonal AC. Ordinary source blue geometry is rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: ABCD is a rhombus with side length 10 cm; BC carries the printed side label. Angle BAD is 60°. AC and BD intersect perpendicularly at X.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied side length, 60° angle, vertex labels and right-angle marker are visible; no calculated lengths or bisected-angle values are supplied.

answer.short:
$AX=5\sqrt3\text{ cm}$.

The diagonals of a rhombus bisect its angles, giving a $30^\circ$ right triangle.
answer.worked:
The diagonals of a rhombus bisect its angles and meet at right angles. Thus $\angle BAX=30^\circ$, $\angle AXB=90^\circ$ and $AB=10\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}\cos30^\circ&=\frac{AX}{10}\\AX&=10\cos30^\circ\\AX&=10\times\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\AX&=5\sqrt3\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
